newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's RIMSA to dispose of Pemex toxic waste.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's RIMSA to dispose of Pemex toxic waste.

text.p: The northern Mexican firm Residuos Industriales Multiquim S.A. (RIMSA) will process 2,000 tonnes out of a total of 7,000 tonnes from a Pemex plant, a company director told Reuters on Monday.

"Pemex called for bids to handle and dispose of 2,000 tonnes of ... hexachlorates. We won and are bringing the (waste) to Mina to transport it to Texas to be incinerated," said Juan A. Cuellar, planning director at RIMSA.
RIMSA will repackage the waste at Mina, in the state of Nuevo Leon, which borders Texas.
The toxic waste was produced at the Pajaritos petrochemical complex in the Gulf of Mexico state of Veracruz, which is run by state-owned oil and gas corporation Pemex.
RIMSA plans to ship the waste to Port Arthur, Texas, to be incinerated by Waste Management International because there are no facilities for incinerating toxic waste in Mexico, Cuellar said.
Mexico's Ecological Balance and Environmental Protection Act was passed in 1988. Before then, firms used to dump toxic waste with impunity, Cuellar said.
RIMSA has a 50 percent share of the Mexican market in toxic waste processing, Cuellar said.
